articles.title: Deshaun Watson tipped for Week 1 starter but pundits project Shedeur Sanders takeover
articles.standfirst: The Browns’ quarterback battle could be far from over even if Watson gets the Week 1 nod
articles.summary: The Browns’ quarterback battle could be far from over even if Watson gets the Week 1 nod
articles.body:
Deshaun Watson appears to have strengthened his case to open the 2026 season as the Cleveland Browns’ starting quarterback, but one prominent prediction suggests Shedeur Sanders could eventually take control of the job.

The Browns entered training camp with Watson and Sanders at the center of their quarterback competition. Head coach Todd Monken has continued to evaluate both players, leaving the door open for either quarterback to claim the job before the regular season begins.

That competition started to tilt toward Watson after he opened Cleveland’s preseason against the Chicago Bears. The veteran played the first half and completed 11 of 15 passes for 126 yards, while Sanders entered after halftime.

Sanders is scheduled to start the Browns’ second preseason game against the Buffalo Bills, giving him another chance to make his case.

Watson’s return is particularly significant after he missed the entire 2025 season following a second Achilles surgery. Before his injury troubles, he was a three-time Pro Bowl quarterback, although his time in Cleveland hasn’t matched the level he reached with the Houston Texans.

Watson now looks like the safer bet to start Week 1. However, that doesn’t mean he’ll necessarily hold the position throughout the campaign.

Sanders could eventually seize control

ESPN Cleveland’s Aaron Goldhammer has made a particularly bold prediction about how the competition could unfold. Goldhammer expects Watson to start the season opener but believes Sanders will eventually start more games and win more games for Cleveland.

“I think Shedeur is going to start the most games and win the most games,” said Goldhammer .

“Although I think Deshaun will start the first game, and the Shedeur fans need to realize just because he isn't starting the first game doesn't mean he won't start the most games, doesn't mean he won't start the most important games, doesn't mean the season by-large won't belong to him, it just means Deshaun is where the season will start for the Browns.”

That scenario would create an intriguing storyline for the Browns. If Watson plays well and Cleveland consistently wins, there’d be little reason for Monken to make a change. But if the offense struggles or Watson fails to rediscover his previous form, Sanders could quickly become an appealing alternative.

There’s also been controversy surrounding the way Cleveland has divided preseason opportunities. Former NFL quarterback Robert Griffin III accused the Browns of putting Sanders at a disadvantage by having him start the second preseason game, potentially without the same first-team support Watson received in the opener.

"I'm convinced the Cleveland Browns never had any intention to start Shedeur Sanders," Griffin writes.

"Shedeur starting the 2nd preseason game without the rest of the Browns starters makes zero sense. It's impossible to get a comparable evaluation in a QB competition if Shedeur doesn't get to play with all the starters."

Still, that doesn’t necessarily mean the Browns have already decided on Watson. Sanders can still force his way into the conversation with strong performances, particularly if he shows enough command of the offense to convince Monken that he gives Cleveland a better chance to win.

Watson remains the logical Week 1 favorite, particularly after receiving the first preseason start. But Goldhammer’s prediction shouldn’t be dismissed. If Watson struggles and Sanders continues developing, the rookie could eventually turn a preseason competition into a changing of the guard.

articles.title: What Shedeur Sanders said about Bills star Josh Allen ahead of pre-season clash
articles.standfirst: Shedeur Sanders has a lot to prove, and he’ll do it against one of the NFL’s best quarterbacks.
articles.summary: Shedeur Sanders has a lot to prove, and he’ll do it against one of the NFL’s best quarterbacks.
articles.body:
S hedeur Sanders will face one of the biggest challenges of his young career this week as he goes up against Josh Allen , the face of the Buffalo Bills and a former NFL MVP, in what could become a turning point in the battle for the starting quarterback job with the Cleveland Browns .

The rookie quarterback will take part in the joint practice between the Browns and Bills, where he will have the opportunity to share the field with a player he has long admired and known.

“Josh Allen, I met him a couple of times in the past through different deals and stuff off the field,” Sanders said. “He always been cool. I always respect him fully. He plays a great game. His style of play fits him perfectly.”

Thursday’s practice in Berea will serve as a demanding test for Cleveland. The Browns’ defense will face one of the NFL’s top quarterbacks , while Sanders will look to continue impressing the coaching staff against a franchise that has reached the playoffs in seven straight seasons.

Shedeur Sanders looks to seize a key opportunity

The joint practice comes after Cleveland’s difficult preseason opener, a 34-10 loss to the Chicago Bears .

Deshaun Watson started that game and completed 11 of 15 passes for 126 yards , leading the Browns’ only two scoring drives, though he also lost a fumble after being sacked on fourth down.

Why Shedeur Sanders may already have lost the Browns QB1 battle to Deshaun Watson

Sanders took over in the second half and finished 6-of-11 passing for 79 yards and an interception . His best play was a 35-yard completion to Luke Floriea on third-and-long, but he was unable to lead the offense into the end zone.

The plan is for Watson and Sanders to split first-team reps during Thursday’s practice before the rookie gets the opportunity to start Saturday’s preseason game.

“I’m truly excited about it,” Sanders said. “They have a great defense, great challenge ahead. I’m just happy to be able to be a part of it.”

Cleveland could rest several starters

All indications are that Sanders will play the first half against Buffalo, although he may do so without several of Cleveland’s regular starters.

Browns head coach Todd Monken and Bills head coach Joe Brady agreed that veteran players could sit out Saturday’s game if they believe they got enough work during Thursday’s joint practice.

If that plan holds, Sanders will play the first half, Deshaun Watson will take over in the third quarter, and Dillon Gabriel will finish the game.

Monken has yet to decide who will be the Browns’ starting quarterback for the season opener, but Thursday’s joint practice and Saturday’s matchup could go a long way toward determining who enters the final week of the preseason with the edge.

The Browns will wrap up their preseason schedule on August 27 against the New England Patriots before opening the regular season on September 13 on the road against the Jacksonville Jaguars .

articles.title: Deshaun Watson in the spotlight following his clash with Cleveland fans
articles.standfirst: The Browns quarterback returns to a fan base still angry over his contract
articles.summary: The Browns quarterback returns to a fan base still angry over his contract
articles.body:
Deshaun Watson has spent much of the NFL offseason insisting that outside noise won't define his return. Cleveland may be about to test that claim in a way practice never could.

The Browns quarterback is expected to be back at Huntington Bank Field with the Buffalo Bills visiting for a preseason game, and local radio host Ken Carman believes the crowd reaction could be jarring.

“He’s about to get a taste of real Cleveland coming up here on Saturday,” Carman said on The Ken Carman Show with Anthony Lima on 92.3 The Fan.

That warning came after Watson dismissed concern over being booed, saying he doesn't care. His history with the fan base suggests the reaction could be impossible to ignore.

The last time Watson played at home was in October 2024, when he suffered a season-ending Achilles injury against the Cincinnati Bengals . He was booed as he left the field, and sections of the crowd have continued to make their feelings clear since then.

Why Browns fans remain angry with Watson

The frustration is rooted in much more than one bad season.

Cleveland traded a huge package, including three first-round picks, to acquire Watson from the Houston Texans in 2022. The franchise then gave him a fully guaranteed five-year, $230 million contract.

Since then, his availability has been limited. Watson missed the first 11 games of 2022 because of an NFL suspension tied to allegations of sexual misconduct during massage sessions. Criminal charges were not filed, but the league suspended him and fined him $5 million.

He then played only six games in 2023 and seven in 2024 before the Achilles injury wiped out his 2025 season. Anthony Lima believes that gap between investment and production is what will fuel the response inside the stadium.

“It might be like culture shock to him,” Lima said. “He’s not getting booed every day in his world. It’s going to be different when he takes the field.”

Shedeur Sanders makes atmosphere more combustible

The quarterback competition has only sharpened the scrutiny.

Many Browns fans have rallied around Shedeur Sanders , while NFL reporter Jason La Canfora has argued that the job has never truly been an even contest.

“The Browns still haven’t declared a starter, but I’m going to let you in on a little secret,” La Canfora said. “Deshaun Watson was always going to be their starting quarterback, unless he got hurt. There’s about 240 million reasons why.”

Watson also helped himself in preseason, completing 11 of 15 passes for 126 yards against the Chicago Bears . Sanders went 6 of 11 for 79 yards with an interception.

Still, Todd Monken has continued to evaluate both quarterbacks publicly.

That makes Saturday important for reasons beyond the depth chart. Watson has said the boos don't matter. Cleveland is about to give him the clearest possible chance to prove it.

articles.title: Is Cleveland's offense in trouble? Quinshon Judkins injury adds to Browns QB uncertainty
articles.standfirst: The Browns have questions everywhere: Judkins’ injury adds another problem to Cleveland’s offense.
articles.summary: The Browns have questions everywhere: Judkins’ injury adds another problem to Cleveland’s offense.
articles.body:
As the Cleveland Browns look to establish an offensive identity under new head coach Todd Monken , running back Quinshon Judkins is expected to become one of the team’s most important pieces. However, before taking on that larger role, Cleveland needs to make sure he can stay healthy.

An injury sidelines Judkins

Judkins missed his second consecutive practice on Thursday after sitting out the team’s joint session with the Buffalo Bills. According to Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com , the running back is dealing with a “nagging” injury that has limited his participation.

While the situation has raised some concerns, Monken downplayed the issue and said keeping Judkins out was mainly a precautionary decision .

“Out of precaution. I think we were smart with where he’s at,” Monken said.

The lack of details surrounding the injury has created some uncertainty about Judkins’ condition, especially since it continues to bother him. Still, the Browns understand the impact their running back can have and, after his rookie season ended early due to injury, they are choosing to be cautious with one of their most important offensive weapons.

Cleveland needs Judkins’ impact

During his rookie campaign, Judkins showed his potential by recording 230 carries for 827 yards and seven touchdowns , ranking among the NFL’s busiest running backs with the 18th-most rushing attempts in the league .

Now with more experience, his role in Monken’s system is expected to grow significantly, especially with Cleveland still searching for answers at quarterback.

Neither Deshaun Watson nor Shedeur Sanders has completely erased doubts, meaning the running game could become Cleveland’s most reliable path to moving the offense forward.

The Browns will continue monitoring Judkins’ progress in the coming days, but they know his availability will be crucial to the team’s hopes as the start of the season approaches.

articles.title: Vince Young warns Shedeur Sanders about the harsh reality of being an NFL quarterback
articles.standfirst: The former NFL star shared a powerful message for the Browns rookie as he navigates criticism, expectations, and the fight for his place in Cleveland.
articles.summary: The former NFL star shared a powerful message for the Browns rookie as he navigates criticism, expectations, and the fight for his place in Cleveland.
articles.body:
The former NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year and No. 3 overall pick entered the league as one of the biggest prospects of his generation. After leading the Texas Longhorns to a national championship victory over the USC Trojans in his final college season, Vince Young lived up to the expectations surrounding his arrival in the NFL: he was named to the Pro Bowl as a rookie and guided the Tennessee Titans to the playoffs in his second season.

He also became the first and only rookie player to appear on the cover of the Madden video game the following year.

However, Young’s NFL journey was defined by intense pressure. The quarterback faced constant criticism due to his inconsistency on the field, his complicated relationship with head coach Jeff Fisher, and the relentless scrutiny from the media. His career ended earlier than expected, with the two-time Pro Bowl selection playing his final NFL game at the age of 28 in 2011 .

Now, the former quarterback is telling his story in a new Netflix documentary as part of the Untold series, a production that chronicles his journey from his days at the University of Texas to the end of his professional career, including brief offseason stints with the Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers, and Buffalo Bills.

At 43 years old, Young also shared a message for current Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders , who has faced heavy criticism since before entering the NFL. The son of Deion Sanders went from being viewed as a potential first-round pick to falling all the way to the fifth round of the 2025 NFL Draft .

“I hate to see what’s going on in Cleveland right now,” Young told Heavy Sports. “I hate to see that quarterbacks gotta prove theirselves each and every year. But it’s like negative energy. It’s not supportive. You know what I mean? I hate to see that.”

Vince Young’s advice for Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson

Young compared Sanders’ situation to some of the most difficult moments of his own career and highlighted the immense pressure young quarterbacks face when expectations are sky-high.

Sanders is currently competing with veteran Deshaun Watson for the starting quarterback job in Cleveland . Watson has also faced criticism due to off-field controversies and is attempting to return as the Browns’ offensive leader after nearly two years away from football because of an Achilles injury.

“When I was in that same position, I felt like that with all the stuff that happened, it’s like you gotta continue to try to change the perception of who you are every time, and you’re actually working your butt off, but you’re also dealing with a heavy load of the whole world talking about you,” Young said.

“In that case, it’s not easy dealing with that. I can tell guys like Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson, just make sure y’all got somebody in your corner that you can talk to — because it is a lot. That is a lot to deal with, and you gotta perform, and you gotta complete that throw, and you gotta be a leader. It is a lot.”

articles.title: Nick Chubb Net Worth: Pro Bowl Browns running back made solid NFL career earnings
articles.standfirst: Chubb spent seven seasons with the Cleveland Browns and one season with the Houston Texans.
articles.summary: Chubb spent seven seasons with the Cleveland Browns and one season with the Houston Texans.
articles.body:
The NFL world is saying goodbye to one of the best running backs of the past eight years. On Friday, Nick Chubb announced that he's retiring from football after eight seasons, seven of which were spent with the Cleveland Browns .

Chubb spent the 2025 season with the Houston Texans . The running back finished his NFL career with four Pro Bowl appearances , and ranks third all-time among running backs in yards per carry (minimum 900 attempts).

Two knee injuries limited Nick Chubb's earning potential, but he still did well

As a 2nd round pick, Chubb was able to secure a solid rookie contract despite having suffered a brutal knee injury in 2015 during his sophomore season at Georgia . Chubb somehow bounced back incredibly from that injury, surpassing 1,1130 rushing yards in each of his last two seasons with the Bulldogs.

The Browns saw enough to make him the 35th overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft . Chubb was able to earn the starting running back job midway through his rookie season and never looked back. He made the Pro Bowl every season from 2019 to 2022 , and was named Second-Team All-Pro in that final season.

Before the 2021 season, Chubb signed his first and last big contract: a three-year, $36.6 million extension . Unfortunately, another major knee injury struck early on during the 2023 season that cut short his year and limited him to only eight games in 2024. Chubb and the Browns parted ways after that season, and the running back signed a one-year, $2.5 million deal with the Houston Texans for the 2025 season .

According to Spotrac , Chubb ended up earning $38.867 million throughout his eight-year NFL career . Chubb's net worth is estimated to be around $22 million , helped by numerous brand partnerships, including with Reign Body Fuel , My Fitness Pal , Abercrombie and more.

articles.title: “Monken doesn't make any decisions”: Ochocinco explains why Browns' owners have final say in QB1 battle
articles.standfirst: Deshaun Watson’s preseason form is improving while Shedeur Sanders faces one final chance to change the QB1 race
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson’s preseason form is improving while Shedeur Sanders faces one final chance to change the QB1 race
articles.body:
The closer the Cleveland Browns get to naming their starting quarterback, the more the debate is shifting away from practice reps and toward the people making the final decision.

Deshaun Watson has built momentum with a strong preseason showing, while Shedeur Sanders continues to make his case for the job.

Yet former NFL receiver Chad “Ochocinco” Johnson believes first-year head coach Todd Monken may not have the decisive voice when Cleveland finally chooses its Week 1 starter.

“But Todd Monken doesn’t make any calls,” Johnson said on Nightcap. “The final say-so comes from the person who signed the check, regardless of what Todd Monken says.”

He added: “You know who’s going to be under center. And I say it again. I say it time and time again. It’s his job to lose.”

Johnson was referring to Watson , whose fully guaranteed five-year, $230 million contract remains one of the biggest factors hanging over the competition.

His claim that ownership will make the final call has not been confirmed by the Browns , although general manager Andrew Berry previously indicated that Cleveland’s head coach would have significant input.

Watson gives Monken reasons to believe

The football argument for Watson has also strengthened. Returning from back-to-back Achilles surgeries, he completed 11 of 15 passes for 126 yards against the Chicago Bears , finishing with a 98.2 passer rating.

He didn't throw an interception, although he lost a fumble after being sacked. Monken came away impressed by more than the statistics.

“What I wanted to see was how comfortable he was leading up to the game, how comfortable he was in the huddle,” Monken said.

Asked whether Watson passed those tests, the coach answered simply: “In my mind he did.”

Monken was even more enthusiastic when discussing the significance of seeing Watson back in live action.

“Oh, it was awesome,” Monken added. “It was so cool to watch him play.”

NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport has also reported that Watson has the “leg up” over Sanders , in part because he's more experienced with Cleveland’s offensive operation.

That advantage is not without concerns. Watson has thrown 12 interceptions across 17 training camp practices, making ball security an obvious issue as the competition reaches its final stage.

Sanders has final opportunity to force issue

Sanders hasn't disappeared from the race. He completed 6 of 11 passes for 79 yards against Chicago , including a 35-yard connection with Luke Floriea , but also threw an interception and finished with a 39.6 passer rating. Monken has nevertheless praised his progress.

“Well, he’s improved so much,” Monken said. “I mean, he really has in terms of climbing the pocket, working through his progressions.”

Sanders is expected to get another significant opportunity against the Buffalo Bills , while Watson will follow later in the game. Monken has also indicated the decision should come early next week.

That leaves the Browns with more than a simple depth-chart choice. They must weigh performance, experience, development and the enormous financial investment already attached to Watson .

Whether Monken truly has the final say remains disputed. What is becoming clearer is that Watson has given Cleveland both football and financial reasons to keep the job in his hands.

Deshaun Watson has built momentum with a strong preseason showing, while Shedeur Sanders continues to make his case for the job.
Yet former NFL receiver Chad “Ochocinco” Johnson believes first-year head coach Todd Monken may not have the decisive voice when Cleveland finally chooses its Week 1 starter.
“But Todd Monken doesn’t make any calls,” Johnson said on Nightcap. “The final say-so comes from the person who signed the check, regardless of what Todd Monken says.”
He added: “You know who’s going to be under center. And I say it again. I say it time and time again. It’s his job to lose.”
Johnson was referring to Watson , whose fully guaranteed five-year, $230 million contract remains one of the biggest factors hanging over the competition.

His claim that ownership will make the final call has not been confirmed by the Browns , although general manager Andrew Berry previously indicated that Cleveland’s head coach would have significant input.

The football argument for Watson has also strengthened. Returning from back-to-back Achilles surgeries, he completed 11 of 15 passes for 126 yards against the Chicago Bears , finishing with a 98.2 passer rating.
He didn't throw an interception, although he lost a fumble after being sacked. Monken came away impressed by more than the statistics.

Asked whether Watson passed those tests, the coach answered simply: “In my mind he did.”
Monken was even more enthusiastic when discussing the significance of seeing Watson back in live action.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson gets fed up with Browns fans and unloads on his own fanbase after dealing with boos
articles.standfirst: Watson is finally letting the ravenous Cleveland Browns fans get to him, and it could mark a turning point in their collective era.
articles.summary: Watson is finally letting the ravenous Cleveland Browns fans get to him, and it could mark a turning point in their collective era.
articles.body:
After the first preseason game, the Cleveland Browns quarterback competition seemed to be very much going in Deshaun Watson 's favor. He played relatively well, while Shedeur Sanders threw a rough interception.

More importantly, head coach Todd Monken liked what he saw from Watson in that first game. The second game, which took place on Saturday against the Buffalo Bills , was a whole other story. Watson struggled mightily, completing just 5-of-12 passes for 36 yards while also throwing an ill-advised interception . But the worst of it all had nothing to do with his performance.

Watson was playing in the second half, alongside backups around him - just as Sanders did in the first game. That didn't stop Browns fans from relentlessly booing Watson, which isn't the first time it's happened . But this time, it very much seems to have emotionally affected Watson.

Deshaun Watson fires back at Cleveland Browns fans who booed him at his worst moments

The 30-year-old spoke to the media after the game about the booing, and showed a frustration towards his own fanbase that hasn't been seen before .

I think you guys know, too. The whole world notices, it has nothing to do about the performance. It's a little bit more personal than that. So I think that's a disrespectful thing. I'm gonna keep whatever I feel with me and my family, internally on how I feel about that... Last time I played on this field I tore my Achilles, and that same fanbase they cheered when I got hurt. What does that have to do with anything about performance?

Watson appeared to be getting slightly emotional while saying those comments. He's clearly been affected by how the city has treated him, especially during his toughest moments.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders shows his class once again in defense of Deshaun Watson: "I don't really appreciate that"
articles.standfirst: Watson had to deal with a rough home game in Week 2 of the preseason, but his Cleveland Browns teammate has his back.
articles.summary: Watson had to deal with a rough home game in Week 2 of the preseason, but his Cleveland Browns teammate has his back.
articles.body:
It has been a preseason to forget for first-year head coach Todd Monken and the Cleveland Browns . After getting crushed 34-10 by the Chicago Bears last week, the Browns got dominated 31-7 by the Buffalo Bills this week, and this time it happened at home in front of their fans.

Those same fans ended up turning into the story of the day. The home fans turned on Deshaun Watson , booing him throughout his appearance in the second half. After the game, Watson spoke about how it's become a "personal" thing against him, and not about performance .

Shedeur Sanders , on the other hand, started the game and played relatively well. He then watched as Watson struggled and the fans made their choice in the quarterback competition clear. Despite that, Sanders getting a leg up in this fashion doesn't sit well with the young quarterback at all .

Shedeur Sanders doesn't appreciate Browns fans booing Deshaun Watson

While speaking to the media after the game, Sanders echoed Watson's comment that it was disrespectful of the fans to boo their quarterback - no matter his history on and off the field .

Just for all the fans, I really appreciate y'all showing up and everything. However y'all feel about the situation with Deshaun and about everything. Still, I think it's more about a bigger purpose than to disrespect. It's just a respect thing that I feel like should be there. Because we're all out there trying to do our best and trying to serve the franchise the best way possible... So I don't really appreciate that.

Despite being in a full-blown, heated quarterback competition, Watson is Sanders' teammate at the end of the day . They both want the best for each other and the team, despite what many might be led to believe.

articles.title: ‘My fault’: Shedeur Sanders owns up to his clumsy rookie mistake in the midst of the battle to become the Browns’ quarterback
articles.standfirst: Cleveland rookie takes responsibility for coin-toss mix-up before delivering a composed preseason performance against Buffalo
articles.summary: Cleveland rookie takes responsibility for coin-toss mix-up before delivering a composed preseason performance against Buffalo
articles.body:
S hedeur Sanders found himself at the centre of attention before he had even taken his first snap for the Cleveland Browns against the Buffalo Bills .

The quarterback, who is competing for a starting role in Cleveland , admitted that he made an awkward mistake before Saturday's preseason matchup when he failed to report for the coin toss despite being named a team captain.

Sanders explained the mix-up during a sideline interview with News 5 Cleveland , taking responsibility rather than trying to hide what happened.

“I messed up before I got on the field,” he said. “I didn’t go out for the coin toss. I know I was the captain, but I just thought I was the captain of the team for a week. I didn’t know I was captain of the coin toss.

“It was a laughing moment with Coach [Todd] Monken and everybody. It was funny. I’m like, ‘My fault, Coach. I thought we were just being situationally aware. I thought you were just informing me on what we’re going to do when it happens.’”

It was an unusual moment for Sanders , particularly because the quarterback is trying to make an impression during a preseason battle that could have major consequences for his immediate future.

Rather than allowing the blunder to become a distraction, however, Sanders quickly shifted his attention toward what mattered most: his performance once the game began.

Sanders responds after difficult outing against Chicago

The Bills game represented an important opportunity for Sanders after a less convincing showing against the Chicago Bears .

His previous preseason appearance included an interception that was widely viewed as an unnecessary mistake, increasing the importance of his next opportunity to demonstrate consistency and command of Cleveland's offense.

Against Buffalo, Sanders showed signs of settling into the role.

After the Bills opened the scoring, the Browns quarterback answered with a touchdown drive that levelled the contest at 7-7 with 2:56 remaining in the opening quarter.

Sanders ultimately completed 9 of 11 passes for 74 yards and a touchdown. He did throw an interception and was sacked, but his overall performance produced an 87.1 passer rating.

The interception was particularly unfortunate. A pass intended for tight end Jermaine Terry arrived slightly behind the receiver, allowing the ball to deflect off Terry's hands and into the arms of Bills safety Damar Hamlin .

Despite the turnover, Cleveland's decision-makers appeared encouraged by Sanders' overall command.

“Really pleased with Shedeur,” Browns general manager Andrew Berry said on the telecast.

“I think everyone can see how well he threw the ball, he played with poise, he played with command of the offense. You could see his playmaking. That fourth-down throw to Blake Whiteheart and then we got a holding penalty on the scramble that he overcame with a nice throw to Luke Floriea.”

Sanders was similarly upbeat when reflecting on his contribution during his mid-game interview.

“My half of the game, it felt great to be back in the stadium,” Sanders said. “It went really great today. I’m real proud of the way how we operated.”

His night ended after the first half, with Deshaun Watson taking over at quarterback.

Watson struggled to generate momentum. He completed just 5 of 12 attempts for 35 yards, throwing one interception without producing a touchdown across four series spanning the third and fourth quarters. Browns supporters also voiced their displeasure by booing Watson during the performance.

That leaves Cleveland's quarterback situation firmly under the spotlight as the preseason moves toward its conclusion.

Sanders still has plenty to prove before any decision is made, but his ability to recover from an embarrassing pregame misunderstanding and deliver a relatively composed performance will be an important part of the conversation.

Head coach Todd Monken has indicated that the Browns do not intend to prolong the decision indefinitely. Speaking before the Bills game on the University Hospitals Browns Radio Network, Monken said he “[does] not anticipate the quarterback decision going past early in next week.”

For Sanders , then, the coin-toss mistake could ultimately become little more than a funny story from his preseason, provided his performances continue to give Cleveland reasons to believe he can handle the much bigger responsibilities that await him.
